headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error exposure: oh-my-openagent can ingest project code and send broad network traffic while dbt-core touches warehouse data and exposes API access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: oh-my-openagent reads project code, AGENTS.md, README.md, and uses runtime-injected MCPs/hooks, so dbt-core content could be treated as instructions if placed in shared files. dbt-core itself has no shared-channel controls or provenance features documented here. The pathway exists in default workspace-style use, but not enough evidence for high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or repository checkout
IF dbt-core outputs are written into files that oh-my-openagent reads as guidance
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable automatic ingestion of AGENTS.md/README.md for the support agent
Require explicit human review before treating file contents as instructions
Use read-only mounts for dbt-core outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent file handoffs

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress; oh-my-openagent touches project code, session history, and provider auth prompts, plus broad egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive warehouse or auth material can flow into the support agent's outbound requests. The blast radius includes exfiltration, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same warehouse-connected workspace
IF provider auth prompts or session history are available to the support agent
IF outbound requests from the support agent include copied context
mitigations: Remove shared filesystem access
Rotate any credentials exposed to the support agent
Restrict the support agent to a redacted workspace copy
Block outbound requests from contexts containing warehouse data
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on agent prompts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core can call a data warehouse API, while oh-my-openagent can run browsers, spawn subprocesses, and use multiple instances with per-installation session scope. That creates overlapping mutable operations and possible contention on shared project files or external resources. No locking is documented, so conflict is plausible in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same project checkout or generated artifacts
IF multiple oh-my-openagent instances run against the same installation
IF dbt-core jobs and browser/subprocess actions target the same mutable resource
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate working directory
Serialize jobs that touch the same project files
Disable multi-instance use for the support agent
Use per-agent credentials for external services
requires-engineering: add file and resource locks around shared writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: oh-my-openagent can ingest project code, AGENTS.md, and session history, then act through browsers, subprocesses, and team_* APIs. dbt-core produces warehouse-facing outputs that the support agent could treat as authoritative without verification. That creates a strong cascade from generated artifacts to downstream actions, with potentially irreversible operational mistakes.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs are forwarded into the support agent without validation
IF the support agent is allowed to send messages or create tasks based on those outputs
IF downstream actions affect production systems or customer communications
mitigations: Require human approval before any team_send_message or team_task_create action
Add a verification step that checks dbt outputs against source data
Limit the support agent to draft-only mode
Log and review all cross-agent handoffs
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for dbt-derived inputs

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while oh-my-openagent touches session history, provider auth prompts, and anonymous telemetry with broad network egress. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, but the mixed data classes and outbound telemetry create a plausible retention/residency mismatch. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes regulated records
IF telemetry or provider auth prompts are retained outside the required jurisdiction
IF the deployment requires a specific retention or residency policy
mitigations: Disable telemetry where possible
Keep regulated data out of the support agent workspace
Review retention settings for both tools
Use separate environments for warehouse and support workflows
requires-engineering: document residency and retention guarantees for both agents
